replaces.AGO: russian_owned_r10.json countries.AGO profits_* (the only AGO rusfirms input)

AGO.profits_note: Cash dividends Alrosa received from Catoca. 2020-2021 from Alrosa's audited IFRS cash flow ('dividends received from associates', Catoca is ~all of it); 2019 estimated (FY2018 dividend at the then 32.8% stake; not found). 2022-2024 zero: FY2021-23 dividends declared but not paid (Alrosa IFRS 2025 note 5.2). 2025: RUB 19,019m cash received in May 2025 for assigning the dividend claims, booked separately from the RUB 15,942m share price (IFRS 2025 note 5.3) - the r10 'high case' happened. 2026 zero (stake sold).

IRQ.profits_note: Profit = remuneration fee (Lukoil's 75% / Gazprom Neft's 30% share, excluding the state partner) less 35% Iraqi income tax; cost-recovery barrels repay costs and are not profit. 2022 and 2023 from Iraq EITI (PCLD tables, reconciled with SOMO): Lukoil 126.25m gross/44.19m tax (2022), 178.69m/62.54m (2023); Gazprom Neft 0 in 2022 (carried forward: cost-recovery ceiling), 33.18m/11.61m (2023). 2019-2021: fee x production (WQ2 146.0 Mbbl and Badra 12.86 Mbbl in 2021, Iraq EITI 2021). 2024 estimated from 2022-23 and ~460 kb/d. 2025: Lukoil paid to ~Q3, force majeure after Oct-2025 sanctions; Gazprom Neft (US-sanctioned Jan 2025) little. 2026: West Qurna-2 handed to Basra Oil Co., settlement amount undisclosed (high case). Rosneft's Kurdistan pipeline (KPC) is NOT included in the main estimate: see alternatives.IRQ_A.

IRQ_A.label: add Rosneft's share of Kurdistan Pipeline Company tariffs (60%, 49% from Nov 2025); cash to Rosneft = 0.5 (0.3-0.8) of its share
IRQ_A.why_not_main: The pipeline was shut from 25 March 2023 to 27 September 2025 because of the ICC arbitration (Iraq v Turkey, filed 2014) and the Baghdad-Erbil dispute, not because of the war; a no-war world would have had the same closure, so measuring it against 2019-2021 would book a war-unrelated drop as a shift toward Ukraine. KPC tariff payments also include capital recovery on Rosneft's ~USD 1.8bn 2017 investment.

KAZ.finding: Kazakhstan EITI 2023-2024 (official) lists dividends paid to the state share of Uranium One's 50/50 JVs: Karatau 48.59bn KZT (2023), 58.85bn (2024); Akbastau 57.15bn (2024). Uranium One's equal share = EUR 0.097bn (2023, Karatau only) and EUR 0.228bn (2024, two JVs) - already above russian_owned_r10's 2024 guess for ALL of Uranium One (central 0.18). South Inkai (U1 70%), Khorasan, Zarechnoye (sold Dec 2024) come on top. Pre-war JV dividends are not in the 2019 / 2020-21 / 2022 EITI reports (they cover production and taxes only); Kazatomprom's annual reports (dividends received from JVs) would give both the pre-war base and the U1 share.

leads.UZB_EGY: eiti.org has no Uzbekistan or Egypt country pages reachable (404 'Not found'); EITI reports show payments to governments, not dividends to foreign owners, so they would bound but not measure Lukoil's (UZB, EGY) and Rosneft's (Zohr) remittances. Not checked further.
leads.VEN_MOZ: No rusfirms part on the site for Venezuela or Mozambique (data.json). Venezuela is not an EITI member (Rosneft's Venezuelan stakes went to Roszarubezhneft in 2020). Rosneft's Mozambique interests are offshore exploration blocks without production, so no profits to send; nothing to add.
leads.ARM: Armenia EITI covers mining; Russian-owned rusfirms there (Gazprom Armenia, banks, South Caucasus Railway) are outside EITI scope.
